Project: Kubernetes. Upgrade being assessed: 1.23 -> 1.29.
This change was introduced in release 1.25. Source: Kubernetes Deprecated API Migration Guide (official_deprecation_notice). Section: Removed APIs by release / v1.25 / Event.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
Notable changes in events.k8s.io/v1: * type is limited to Normal and Warning * involvedObject is renamed to regarding * action, reason, reportingController, and reportingInstance are required when creating new events.k8s.io/v1 Events * use eventTime instead of the deprecated firstTimestamp field (which is renamed to deprecatedFirstTimestamp and not permitted in new events.k8s.io/v1 Events) * use series.lastObservedTime instead of the deprecated lastTimestamp field (which is renamed to deprecatedLastTimestamp and not permitted in new events.k8s.io/v1 Events) * use series.count instead of the deprecated count field (which is renamed to deprecatedCount and not permitted in new events.k8s.io/v1 Events) * use reportingController instead of the deprecated source.component field (which is renamed to deprecatedSource.component and not permitted in new events.k8s.io/v1 Events) * use reportingInstance instead of the deprecated source.host field (which is renamed to deprecatedSource.host and not permitted in new events.k8s.io/v1 Events)
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
Removed APIs by release / v1.25 / Event: The events.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version of Event is no longer served as of v1.25. Migrate manifests and API clients to use the events.k8s.io/v1 API version, available since v1.19. All existing persisted objects are accessible via the new API Notable changes in events.k8s.io/v1: * type is limited to Normal and Warning * involvedObject is renamed to regarding * action, reason, reportingController, and reportingInstance are required when creating new events.k8s.io/v1 Events * use eventTime instead of the deprecated firstTimestamp field (which is renamed to deprecatedFirstTimestamp and not permitted in new events.k8s.io/v1 Events) * use series.lastObservedTime instead of the deprecated lastTimestamp field (which is renamed to deprecatedLastTimestamp and not permitted in new events.k8s.io/v1 Events) * use series.count instead of the deprecated count field (which is renamed to deprecatedCount and not permitted in new events.k8s.io/v1 Events) * use reportingController instead of the deprecated source.component field (which is renamed to deprecatedSource.component and not permitted in new events.k8s.io/v1 Events) * use reportingInstance instead of the deprecated source.host field (which is renamed to deprecatedSource.host and not permitted in new events.k8s.io/v1 Events)
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 1.29 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 1.25 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: Event field changes when migrating from events.k8s.io/v1beta1 to events.k8s.io/v1
paths.description: events.k8s.io/v1beta1 Event is no longer served as of v1.25. Manifests and API clients must migrate to events.k8s.io/v1, whose Event schema differs: type is limited to Normal and Warning, involvedObject is renamed to regarding, action/reason/reportingController/reportingInstance are required on creation, and deprecated fields (firstTimestamp, lastTimestamp, count, source.component, source.host) are not permitted in new events.k8s.io/v1 Events.

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 1.25, where events.k8s.io/v1beta1 Event stops being served (upgrade from 1.23 to 1.29).
quotes: The events.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version of Event is no longer served as of v1.25.
conditions.relevance: Ties the removal of the v1beta1 Event API to release 1.25, which is crossed by the 1.23 -> 1.29 upgrade.

conditions.statement: Manifests or API clients reference the events.k8s.io/v1beta1 Event API version.
quotes: Migrate manifests and API clients to use the events.k8s.io/v1 API version
conditions.relevance: Manifests and clients using the removed API version will fail against the 1.25+ API server.

conditions.statement: Code that creates events via events.k8s.io/v1 uses the old field names such as involvedObject, firstTimestamp, lastTimestamp, count, source.component or source.host, or omits required fields action, reason, reportingController, reportingInstance.
quotes: action, reason, reportingController, and reportingInstance are required when creating new events.k8s.io/v1 Events
conditions.relevance: Moving to events.k8s.io/v1 requires updating field names and populating required fields, otherwise creation of new Events is rejected or misbehaves.

conditions.statement: Events created by the application use a type value other than Normal or Warning.
quotes: type is limited to Normal and Warning
conditions.relevance: events.k8s.io/v1 restricts type to Normal and Warning.
ambiguities: The text does not state what happens when another type value is used.

suggested_actions: Migrate manifests and API clients from events.k8s.io/v1beta1 to events.k8s.io/v1 (available since v1.19).
Populate action, reason, reportingController and reportingInstance when creating new events.k8s.io/v1 Events.

Use eventTime instead of firstTimestamp, series.lastObservedTime instead of lastTimestamp, series.count instead of count, reportingController instead of source.component, and reportingInstance instead of source.host.
Restrict Event type to Normal or Warning.
